title: Mapping Eco-Affective Health: A Spatial Framework for Climate-Related Emotional Responses and Mental Health in Urban Systems
content: Urban environments concentrate spatially distributed stressors, including heat, noise, pollution, and biodiversity loss, that are increasingly recognized as determinants of population mental health. However, current approaches rarely integrate environmental structure, lived exposure, and climate-related emotional responses within a unified spatial framework applicable to public health. This article introduces Eco-Affective Health as a spatially explicit framework for understanding how environmental conditions shape climate-related emotional responses, including eco-anxiety, solastalgia, and ecological grief, across urban socio-ecological systems. Drawing on evidence from spatial epidemiology, landscape ecology, environmental mental health, and digital phenotyping, we argue that affective responses to environmental stressors are not randomly distributed but exhibit spatial clustering in relation to environmental exposures, landscape configuration, and mobility-based interactions. We propose the Eco-Affective Health Mapping (EAHM) framework, which integrates four spatial layers: environmental exposures, landscape configuration, person-place interaction, and affective indicators. By conceptualizing climate-related emotional responses as measurable public health signals, EAHM enables the identification of spatial gradients of vulnerability and resilience across urban populations. This framework supports a shift toward prevention-oriented, population-level mental health strategies aligned with planetary health and sustainable development agendas.
